ei.subject: 공통영어1 천재(조수경)
ei.lesson: How Fashion Items Got Their Names
ei.title: How Fashion Items Got Their Names

fullPassage:
Have you ever wondered how fashion items got their names? Many of these names have interesting histories behind them. The jumpsuit, for example, began as clothing designed for people who jumped from planes. Over time, it transformed from practical workwear into a luxury fashion item. Who would have guessed that an outfit once meant for skydiving would become a must-have in high-end fashion?

Sneakers got their name from the word "sneak." Unlike traditional leather-soled shoes, which made a loud sound on hard surfaces, rubber-soled shoes allowed people to walk quietly, or "sneak up" on others. The rubber soles made little noise, and this sneaky quality gave them the name "sneakers."

Blue jeans have a surprisingly international origin. The word "jean" comes from Genoa, Italy, where a tough cotton cloth was produced. This cloth was called "bleu de G\u00EAnes," meaning "blue of Genoa." During the 17th and 18th centuries, this durable fabric was widely traded and eventually became the material we now know as denim, used to make the classic blue jeans we wear today.

The tuxedo has an ironic origin story. It is named after Tuxedo Park, a wealthy community in New York. At a formal event there, a man showed up wearing a short jacket without tails, which was quite different from the traditional long-tailed coats worn at the time. Rather than being rejected, the man's bold fashion choice fascinated the other guests. The shorter jacket quickly became popular and replaced the longer version, and it came to be known as the "tuxedo."

Flip-flops are believed to be among the oldest shoes in history, dating back to around 4,000 BC in ancient Egypt. Their modern name comes from the sound their rubber soles make when they hit the ground — "flip-flop." Interestingly, they are called by different names around the world: "zories" in Japan and "jandals" in New Zealand.

Have you ever heard of Personal Color? It is a method of determining which colors suit you best based on your skin tone. People are generally divided into two categories: warm tones and cool tones. Warm-toned individuals tend to look better in earthy colors like orange, yellow, and brown, while cool-toned people are more suited to colors like blue, purple, and silver. By understanding your personal color, you can make better fashion choices that highlight your natural beauty.

questions.passage: Unlike traditional leather-soled shoes, __________ made a loud sound on hard surfaces, rubber-soled shoes allowed people to walk quietly, or "sneak up" on others. The rubber soles made little noise, and this sneaky quality gave them the name "sneakers."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 leather-soled shoes(사물)를 수식하면서 뒤에 동사 made의 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ which: 사물 선행사(leather-soled shoes) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① what: 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 불가
❌ ② who: 사람 선행사용 → shoes는 사물
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 하나, made의 주어 필요
det.tip: 선행사(사물) + which + 동사: 사물을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: The jumpsuit, for example, began as clothing __________ for people who jumped from planes. Over time, it transformed from practical workwear into a luxury fashion item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: clothing은 디자인되는 대상(수동)이므로 과거분사 designed가 적절하다. "비행기에서 뛰어내리는 사람들을 위해 디자인된 의류"
det.analysis:
✅ ② designed: 과거분사(수동) → clothing이 디자인되는 대상
❌ ① designing: 현재분사(능동) → clothing이 스스로 디자인하는 것이 아님
❌ ③ to design: to부정사 → 목적 표현에 부적절한 문맥
❌ ④ design: 동사원형 → 문법적으로 불가
det.tip: 명사 + p.p.(과거분사): 명사가 동작을 당하는 관계 → 수동의 의미

questions.passage: Have you ever heard of Personal Color? It is a method of __________ which colors suit you best based on your skin tone. People are generally divided into two categories: warm tones and cool tones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 determining이 적절하다. "어떤 색이 가장 잘 어울리는지 결정하는 방법"
det.analysis:
✅ ① determining: 전치사 of + 동명사(~ing)
❌ ② determined: 과거분사 → 전치사 뒤 형태 부적절
❌ ③ to determine: to부정사 → a method of 뒤에 to부정사는 부적절
❌ ④ determine: 동사원형 → 전치사 뒤 불가
det.tip: 전치사(of, for, in, by 등) + 동명사(~ing): 전치사 뒤에는 명사/동명사

questions.passage: At a formal event there, a man showed up ①<u>wearing</u> a short jacket without tails, which was quite different from the traditional long-tailed coats ②<u>wearing</u> at the time. Rather than ③<u>being rejected</u>, the man's bold fashion choice fascinated the other guests.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② wearing → worn: 전통적인 긴 코트는 입혀지는 것(수동)이므로 과거분사 worn이 적절하다. "그 당시에 착용되었던 전통적인 긴 코트"
det.analysis:
❌ ② wearing(능동) → worn(수동): coats는 사람이 입는 대상이므로 수동(worn)
✅ ① wearing: 현재분사(능동) → "짧은 재킷을 입고 있는 남자" (남자가 입는 것)
✅ ③ being rejected: 동명사 수동 → "거부당하는 것" Rather than 뒤 적절
det.tip: 현재분사(~ing) = 능동/진행, 과거분사(p.p.) = 수동/완료. 주어/선행사가 동작의 대상이면 p.p.

questions.passage: Flip-flops are believed to be among the ①<u>oldest</u> shoes in history, dating back to around 4,000 BC in ancient Egypt. Their modern name comes from the sound their rubber soles make when they ②<u>hit</u> the ground. Interestingly, they are ③<u>calling</u> by different names around the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ calling → called: 플립플롭은 불리는 것(수동)이므로 "are called"가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ calling(능동) → called(수동): "they are called" = "그것들은 불린다" (수동태)
✅ ① oldest: 최상급 → "가장 오래된 신발" 올바름
✅ ② hit: 현재시제 → 시간의 부사절(when)에서 현재시제 적절
det.tip: be + p.p. = 수동태. "~라고 불린다" = are called (not are calling)

questions.passage: Sneakers got their name from the word "sneak." Unlike traditional leather-soled shoes, which made a loud sound on hard surfaces, rubber-soled shoes allowed people to walk quietly, or "sneak up" on others. The rubber soles made little noise, and this sneaky quality gave them the name "sneakers."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "The rubber soles made little noise, and this sneaky quality gave them the name 'sneakers'" → 고무 밑창이 소리를 적게 내서 sneakers라는 이름이 붙었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 고무 밑창이 소리를 적게 냄 → sneakers 이름 유래: 본문과 일치
❌ ① jumpsuit은 비행기에서 뛰어내리는 사람을 위한 것 (수영 ✗)
❌ ③ jean은 Genoa(이탈리아)에서 유래 (파리 ✗)
❌ ④ tuxedo는 꼬리 없는 짧은 재킷 (긴 꼬리 코트 ✗)
det.tip: 내용 일치: 각 선택지의 핵심 키워드를 본문과 정확히 대조

ch: Sneakers라는 이름은 고무 밑창이 소리를 적게 내는 것에서 유래했다.
Tuxedo는 긴 꼬리가 달린 전통 코트를 가리키는 이름이다.

questions.passage: Blue jeans have a surprisingly international origin. The word "jean" comes from Genoa, Italy, where a tough cotton cloth was produced. This cloth was called "bleu de G\u00EAnes," meaning "blue of Genoa." During the 17th and 18th centuries, this durable fabric was widely traded and eventually became the material we now know as denim, used to make the classic blue jeans we wear today.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "During the 17th and 18th centuries, this durable fabric was widely traded" → 17~18세기에 거래됨. "19세기에 처음 거래"는 본문과 불일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 19세기에 처음 거래 → 본문은 17~18세기(17th and 18th centuries)
✅ ① 제노바에서 생산: "Genoa, Italy, where a tough cotton cloth was produced" → 일치
✅ ② "bleu de Gênes" = blue of Genoa: 본문과 일치
✅ ④ 데님: "became the material we now know as denim" → 일치
det.tip: 불일치 문제: 시대/숫자/장소 등 구체적 정보를 본문과 정확히 대조

ch: Blue jeans의 원료인 천은 이탈리아 제노바에서 생산되었다.
Blue jeans의 원단은 데님으로 알려져 있다.

questions.passage: Have you ever wondered how fashion items got their names? Many of these names have interesting histories behind them. The jumpsuit, for example, began as clothing designed for people who jumped from planes. Over time, it transformed from practical workwear into a luxury fashion item. Who would have guessed that an outfit once meant for skydiving would become a must-have in high-end fashion?
questions.stem: 이 글(본문 전체)의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "Have you ever wondered how fashion items got their names? Many of these names have interesting histories behind them." → 패션 아이템의 이름에 담긴 흥미로운 유래가 글의 주제.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 이름에 담긴 흥미로운 유래: 제목 "How Fashion Items Got Their Names"와 일치
❌ ① 제작 과정/기술: 언급 없음
❌ ② 현대 패션 트렌드: 글은 유래에 대한 것
❌ ④ 전통 의상/문화적 의미: 글의 초점이 아님
❌ ⑤ 패션 산업/경제: 언급 없음
det.tip: 글의 주제: 제목과 첫 문단의 핵심 질문이 단서 → "how fashion items got their names"

ch: 패션 아이템의 이름에 담긴 흥미로운 유래
세계 각국의 전통 의상과 문화적 의미

questions.passage: Unlike traditional leather-soled shoes, which made a loud sound on hard surfaces, rubber-soled shoes allowed people to walk quietly, or "sneak up" on others. The rubber soles made little noise, and this __________ gave them the name "sneakers."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고무 밑창이 소리를 적게 내어 몰래 다가갈 수 있는 몰래 접근하는 특성(sneaky quality)이 sneakers라는 이름을 만들었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ sneaky quality: "sneak up" + "made little noise" → 몰래 접근하는 특성
❌ ① fashionable appearance: 외모가 아닌 소리 특성이 핵심
❌ ② expensive material: 비싼 재료는 언급되지 않음
❌ ④ heavy weight: 무게는 무관
det.tip: 빈칸 앞의 "this"가 가리키는 내용을 이전 문장에서 찾기 → "walk quietly" = sneaky

questions.passage: At a formal event there, a man showed up wearing a short jacket without tails, which was quite different from the traditional long-tailed coats worn at the time. Rather than being rejected, the man's bold fashion choice __________ the other guests. The shorter jacket quickly became popular and replaced the longer version.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 거부당하는 대신(Rather than being rejected) 다른 손님들을 매료시켰다(fascinated). 이후 짧은 재킷이 인기를 얻은 것이 근거.
det.analysis:
✅ ② fascinated: "Rather than being rejected" + "quickly became popular" → 매료시킴
❌ ① disappointed(실망시킴): 인기를 얻은 결과와 모순
❌ ③ confused(혼란시킴): 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ frightened(두렵게 함): 패션 맥락과 무관
det.tip: Rather than A, B: A가 아니라 B → rejected의 반대 방향인 긍정적 반응

questions.passage: People are generally divided into two categories: warm tones and cool tones. Warm-toned individuals tend to look better in earthy colors like orange, yellow, and brown, while cool-toned people are more suited to colors like blue, purple, and silver. By understanding your personal color, you can make better fashion choices that __________ your natural beauty.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 퍼스널 컬러를 이해하면 자신의 자연스러운 아름다움을 부각시키는(highlight) 패션 선택을 할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① highlight(부각하다): 어울리는 색을 찾아 아름다움을 돋보이게 함
❌ ② hide(숨기다): 아름다움을 숨기는 것이 아님
❌ ③ damage(손상하다): 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): 문맥과 반대
det.tip: "make better fashion choices" → 긍정적 결과를 나타내는 동사 필요

questions.passage: The jumpsuit, for example, began as clothing designed for people who jumped from planes. Over time, it transformed from __________ (practice) workwear into a luxury fashion item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: practice(명사/동사) → practical(형용사): 명사 workwear를 수식하는 형용사가 필요. "실용적인 작업복"
det.analysis:
practice(명사/동사) → practical(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 workwear(명사)를 수식하는 형용사가 필요
practical workwear = 실용적인 작업복
det.tip: practice(동사/명사) → practical(형용사): 명사 앞에서 수식할 때 형용사형 사용

questions.passage: The word "jean" comes from Genoa, Italy, where a tough cotton cloth was produced. This cloth was known for its __________ (durable) and was widely traded during the 17th and 18th centuries.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: durable(형용사) → durability(명사): 소유격 its 뒤에는 명사가 와야 한다. "그것의 내구성"
det.analysis:
durable(형용사) → durability(명사)
소유격(its) + 명사 구조 → durability(내구성)
known for its durability = 내구성으로 유명한
det.tip: 소유격(my, his, its 등) + 명사: 소유격 뒤에는 반드시 명사가 온다

questions.passage: Blue jeans have a surprisingly international origin. The word "jean" comes from Genoa, Italy, where a tough cotton cloth was produced. This cloth was called "bleu de G\u00EAnes," meaning "blue of Genoa." During the 17th and 18th centuries, this durable fabric was widely traded and eventually became the material we now know as denim, used to make the classic blue jeans we wear today.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 blue jeans의 재료가 된 튼튼한 면직물(tough cotton cloth)이 생산된 이탈리아 도시 이름을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "The word 'jean' comes from Genoa, Italy, where a tough cotton cloth was produced" → 제노바 = Genoa
det.analysis:
jean의 어원 = Genoa (이탈리아 제노바)
tough cotton cloth가 생산된 곳 = Genoa, Italy
det.tip: "본문에서 찾기" 유형: 한글 힌트의 키워드와 대응하는 영어 표현을 정확히 찾기

questions.passage: The tuxedo has an ironic origin story. It is named after Tuxedo Park, a wealthy community in New York. At a formal event there, a man showed up wearing a short jacket without tails, which was quite different from the traditional long-tailed coats worn at the time. Rather than being rejected, the man's bold fashion choice fascinated the other guests. The shorter jacket quickly became popular and replaced the longer version, and it came to be known as the "tuxedo."
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 턱시도 파크의 남자가 입은 재킷에 없었던 것을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "a man showed up wearing a short jacket without tails" → 꼬리(뒷자락) = tails
det.analysis:
without tails = 꼬리(뒷자락) 없이
전통 코트는 long-tailed coats → 남자의 재킷은 tails가 없었음
det.tip: without + 명사: ~없이. 질문의 "없었던 것" = without 뒤의 명사

questions.passage: The tuxedo has an ironic origin story. It is named after Tuxedo Park, a wealthy community in New York. At a formal event there, a man showed up wearing a short jacket without tails, which was quite different from the traditional long-tailed coats worn at the time. Rather than being rejected, the man's bold fashion choice fascinated the other guests. The shorter jacket quickly became popular and replaced the longer version, and it came to be known as the "tuxedo."
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 턱시도(짧은 재킷)가 대체한 것을 본문에서 3단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "The shorter jacket quickly became popular and replaced the longer version" → 더 긴 버전(기존의 긴 코트) = the longer version
det.analysis:
replaced + 목적어 = 대체한 것
The shorter jacket replaced the longer version
→ 짧은 재킷이 긴 버전을 대체함
det.tip: replace A: A를 대체하다 → replaced 뒤의 목적어가 대체된 대상

questions.passage: Have you ever wondered how fashion items got their names? Many of these names have interesting histories behind them. The jumpsuit, for example, began as clothing designed for people who jumped from planes. Over time, it transformed from practical workwear into a luxury fashion item. Who would have guessed that an outfit once meant for skydiving would become a must-have in high-end fashion?
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The jumpsuit was originally designed for people who jumped from planes."

det.korean: "The jumpsuit, for example, began as clothing designed for people who jumped from planes." → 본문과 정확히 일치 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "began as clothing designed for people who jumped from planes" = 진술과 동일한 의미
det.tip: 본문의 핵심 내용을 그대로 재진술한 경우 → True

questions.passage: The tuxedo has an ironic origin story. It is named after Tuxedo Park, a wealthy community in New York. At a formal event there, a man showed up wearing a short jacket without tails, which was quite different from the traditional long-tailed coats worn at the time. Rather than being rejected, the man's bold fashion choice fascinated the other guests. The shorter jacket quickly became popular and replaced the longer version, and it came to be known as the "tuxedo."
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The man who wore the short jacket at Tuxedo Park was rejected by the other guests."

det.korean: 본문: "Rather than being rejected, the man's bold fashion choice fascinated the other guests." → 거부당한 것이 아니라 매료시켰다. 따라서 False.
det.analysis:
❌ False: "Rather than being rejected" = 거부당하는 대신 → 실제로는 거부당하지 않았음
